name: Daily Pivot S1/R1 contrarian reversal (higher-TF level gate)
timeframe: level computed on DAILY OHLC; entry evaluated on 30m
condition: Compute classic floor-trader pivots from the PRIOR completed daily bar: P=(Dhigh+Dlow+Dclose)/3; S1=2*P-Dhigh; R1=2*P-Dlow; S2=P-(Dhigh-Dlow); R2=P+(Dhigh-Dlow). On 30m bars within that day: reversal_long when 30m low touches/penetrates S1 (i.e. low<=S1 and close>S1, price approaching support from above); reversal_short when 30m high touches/penetrates R1 (high>=R1 and close<R1). Profit objective is mean-reversion back to P. Use S2/R2 as the harder extreme variant. Gate is: only take a 30m UP bet near S1, only DOWN near R1.
direction: reversal_long at S1 / reversal_short at R1 (also usable as a gate: suppress longs above P-zone, shorts below)
claimed_winrate: none quantified in source; author frames it as a bias tool ('approaching resistance -> bearish bias; support -> bullish bias') and as a reversal-entry whose exit target is the Pivot
sample_or_caveat: Sofien computes pivots midnight-to-midnight Paris time and explicitly flags FX timezone choice as material; choice of daily session boundary will move S1/R1. He charts hourly off daily levels, so 30m is a natural fit. No backtest stats given.
pandas_impl:
# daily30 = 30m OHLC indexed by tz-aware DatetimeIndex (Paris session)
# 1) build prior-day levels causally
d = df.resample('1D').agg({'high':'max','low':'min','close':'last'})
P  = (d['high']+d['low']+d['close'])/3
prev = pd.DataFrame({'P':P,
   'S1':2*P-d['high'],'R1':2*P-d['low'],
   'S2':P-(d['high']-d['low']),'R2':P+(d['high']-d['low'])}).shift(1)  # prior day only -> causal
# 2) map each 30m bar to its day and merge prior-day levels
lev = prev.reindex(df.index.normalize()).set_index(df.index)
rev_long  = (df['low']  <= lev['S1']) & (df['close'] > lev['S1'])
rev_short = (df['high'] >= lev['R1']) & (df['close'] < lev['R1'])

name: Normalized-distance-from-MA overextension release (overextension exhaustion gate)
timeframe: designed on any TF; apply MA on 30m or on a higher TF (1h/4h) and gate the 30m bet
condition: dist = abs(close - SMA(close,200)). norm = 100*(dist - rolling_min(dist,50)) / (rolling_max(dist,50)-rolling_min(dist,50)). LONG when norm drops below 100 having EQUALLED 100 on the prior bar (norm[t]<100 & norm[t-1]==100) AND close[t] < close[t-5] AND close[t] < SMA200[t] (price below MA, max-stretch just released, still falling -> snapback up). SHORT when norm[t]<100 & norm[t-1]==100 AND close[t] > close[t-5] AND close[t] > SMA200[t]. Variant 152644052 uses lookback_ma=300 and a 0-1 normalization (drops from 1 after ==1).
direction: reversal_long / reversal_short (overextension exhaustion). Also strong as a pure GATE: only allow a mean-revert bet when the stretch-from-MA has just hit its 50-bar max and turned.
sample_or_caveat: Signal fires the bar AFTER the distance peaks (norm==100 then <100), so it is causal by construction. Rare trigger (needs distance to set a fresh 50-bar max then contract). The MA(200) on 30m ~= 100h lookback; running MA on 1h/4h makes it a genuine higher-TF overextension gate. Author gives no hit-rate.
source: post:96702773 (code:1 ma/normalized_index, code:2 signal); variant post:152644052
pandas_impl:
ma = close.rolling(200).mean()
dist = (close - ma).abs()
lo = dist.rolling(50).min(); hi = dist.rolling(50).max()
norm = 100*(dist - lo)/(hi - lo)
at_max_prev = norm.shift(1).round(6).eq(100)  # was at 50-bar max last bar
rev_long  = (norm < 100) & at_max_prev & (close < close.shift(5)) & (close < ma)
rev_short = (norm < 100) & at_max_prev & (close > close.shift(5)) & (close > ma)

name: 20-period return-autocorrelation extreme (persistence-cooldown reversal)
timeframe: 20-bar window on the trading TF (use 30m, or compute on 1h/4h as a higher-TF cooldown gate)
condition: Compute Pearson correlation over a 20-bar window between this bar's simple return r[t]=close/close[-1]-1 and the 1-lagged return r[t-1]. When ac20 >= 0.70 (high persistence/trending), expect a pause: LONG if the market is currently DROPPING (close<close[-1]), SHORT if RISING (close>close[-1]). Looser variant uses the 0.50 threshold. Target is only a 'small reaction', not a full reversal.
direction: reversal_long (when falling) / reversal_short (when rising) -- contrarian against an over-persistent move
claimed_winrate: none quantified ('a contrarian strategy may be established'; target = small upside/downside reaction only)
sample_or_caveat: Direction is counter to recent bar move, conditioned on high autocorrelation = trend over-persistence due for a cooldown. Causal: corr uses window ending at t. shift_degree=1 in source. 0.70 is the strong/rarer trigger; 0.50 fires more often. Pairs naturally as a GATE on top of any reversal trigger (only fire reversals when ac20>=0.70).
pandas_impl:
r = close.pct_change()
ac20 = r.rolling(20).corr(r.shift(1))   # causal 20-bar autocorr(lag1)
rising  = close > close.shift(1)
rev_short = (ac20 >= 0.70) & rising
rev_long  = (ac20 >= 0.70) & ~rising
# looser: replace 0.70 with 0.50

name: RSI 'range-reversal' 55-bar memory gate
timeframe: single TF (built on hourly in source); use as a 30m gate or evaluate the 55-bar memory on 30m (~27.5h) or a higher TF
condition: Take a conservative RSI reversal signal (e.g. RSI(14) exits oversold: crosses back above 30; or exits overbought: crosses back below 70). VALIDATE it only if the RSI value 55 bars ago confirms the longer regime: bullish signal valid ONLY if RSI[t-55] > 50; bearish signal valid ONLY if RSI[t-55] < 50. Variant: require ANY RSI value within the last 55 bars to satisfy the >50 / <50 condition.
direction: gate (filters RSI reversal entries; long-side gate needs RSI[t-55]>50, short-side needs RSI[t-55]<50)
sample_or_caveat: This is a NOT-yet-tried flag-value gate: a single historical RSI reading 55 bars back used as a regime filter on a present reversal. Distinct from EMA trend-confluence (it is RSI-of-the-past, not a price MA). 55 is a Fibonacci lookback. No hit-rate given.
pandas_impl:
# rsi = Wilder RSI(14). base conservative signals:
long_raw  = (rsi.shift(1) < 30) & (rsi >= 30)
short_raw = (rsi.shift(1) > 70) & (rsi <= 70)
long_ok  = long_raw  & (rsi.shift(55) > 50)
short_ok = short_raw & (rsi.shift(55) < 50)
# variant: (rsi.shift(1).rolling(55).max() > 50) etc.

name: RSI V-reversal: one-bar exit then re-entry from extreme
condition: Using RSI(8): BULLISH ('V') when current RSI is >15 and <50, the PREVIOUS RSI was <15, and the one before that was >15 (a single-bar dip through the 15 floor and back). BEARISH ('inverted V') when current RSI <85 and >50, previous RSI >85, the one before that <85.
claimed_winrate: none quantified ('extreme values signal a reaction that can be exploited')
sample_or_caveat: A precise 3-bar shape gate on RSI(8), not a static threshold cross -> different from the already-null RSI<20/>80. Thresholds 15/85 are deep. Causal (uses t, t-1, t-2). No backtest stat.
source: post:142385630 (V reversal); related sequence variant post:142138160
pandas_impl:
# rsi = RSI(8)
bull_v = (rsi>15)&(rsi<50)&(rsi.shift(1)<15)&(rsi.shift(2)>15)
bear_v = (rsi<85)&(rsi>50)&(rsi.shift(1)>85)&(rsi.shift(2)<85)

name: RSI/Stochastic pull-back 'ping-pong' comeback band
timeframe: single TF; built with 5-period RSI / 5-period stochastic
condition: LONG: RSI(5) surpasses the 20 oversold level, does NOT exceed a 33 threshold, then comes back DOWN to settle in the [30,33] band -> buy. SHORT: RSI(5) breaks the 80 overbought level, does NOT drop below 67, then comes back UP to the [67,80] band -> sell. (Stochastic variant post:90255632: oversold 20, threshold 30, band [20,30].)
direction: reversal_long / reversal_short (failed continuation off an extreme)
sample_or_caveat: Captures a failed thrust that stalls between the extreme and a nearby threshold then retraces -- a distinct multi-step path condition, not a single cross. Requires tracking that RSI exited the extreme but stayed under/over the threshold band. No hit-rate.
pandas_impl:
# rsi=RSI(5). long: crossed up >20 recently, max since then <33, now in [30,33]
exited_os = (rsi.shift(1) <= 20) & (rsi > 20)
grp = exited_os.cumsum()
max_since = rsi.groupby(grp).cummax()
long_sig = (max_since < 33) & rsi.between(30,33) & (grp>0)
exited_ob = (rsi.shift(1) >= 80) & (rsi < 80)
grp2 = exited_ob.cumsum(); min_since = rsi.groupby(grp2).cummin()
short_sig = (min_since > 67) & rsi.between(67,80) & (grp2>0)

name: RSI divergence GATED by 800-period MA trend
timeframe: RSI/divergence on entry TF; 800-period SMA acts as the higher-TF trend filter (800x30m ~= 16 trading days)
condition: Detect a classic RSI divergence: bullish = price makes a lower low while RSI(13 or 21) makes a higher low, both with RSI near 30; bearish = price higher high while RSI lower high, RSI near 70. GATE: only take bullish divergence when close > SMA(close,800); only take bearish divergence when close < SMA(close,800). (i.e. trade divergences only WITH the long-term MA regime.)
direction: reversal_long (bullish div above 800MA) / reversal_short (bearish div below 800MA)
claimed_winrate: none quantified here; a sibling stochastic-divergence study (41301281) reports the divergence signal had 'more than 50% right directional 13 price bars after the signal'
sample_or_caveat: The novelty vs your null list is the 800-MA REGIME GATE on the divergence (and that divergences are 'preferably considered when the indicator is around extremes' i.e. RSI near 30/70). Author cautions divergences 'are unlikely to provide a winning strategy on their own.' Use the divergence() detector with width window for the swing search.
source: post:47250832 (code:13 divergence detector, entry rule); 13-bar stat from post:41301281

name: True-high/true-low single-bar reversal (K's candlestick reversal)
condition: BULLISH reversal bar: close[t] < close[t-1] (lower close vs prior) AND close[t] > open[t] (bar closed green) AND low[t] < true_low(t-2), where true_low = min(low, prev_close) i.e. low[t] < min(low[t-2], close[t-3]). BEARISH reversal bar: close[t] > close[t-1] AND close[t] < open[t] AND high[t] > true_high(t-2) = max(high[t-2], close[t-3]). A separate 3-3 variant: bullish when 3 consecutive bullish candles follow 3 consecutive bearish candles (and vice-versa).
sample_or_caveat: Uses Welles-Wilder true high/low (incorporates prior close) two bars back -> a stricter undercut/overshoot than raw high/low; NOT in your null list. Causal. Author treats candlestick-only systems as 'unstable' alone -> best as a confluence component (e.g. fire only at daily S1/R1 or at the normalized-distance release).
pandas_impl:
tl2 = pd.concat([low.shift(2), close.shift(3)], axis=1).min(axis=1)  # true low 2 bars back
th2 = pd.concat([high.shift(2), close.shift(3)], axis=1).max(axis=1)
bull_rev = (close < close.shift(1)) & (close > open_) & (low  < tl2)
bear_rev = (close > close.shift(1)) & (close < open_) & (high > th2)

name: Kangaroo Tail reversal GATED by 200-period MA regime
timeframe: candle on entry TF; 200-period SMA as higher-TF regime filter
condition: BULLISH Kangaroo Tail: open and close both in the UPPER third of the bar -> open > low + 0.66*(high-low) AND close > low + 0.66*(high-low); open and close inside the prior bar's range -> low[1] < open,close < high[1]; range expanding -> (high-low) > range[t-1] AND > range[t-2]; and a 200-bar location filter close < close[t-200] (price below where it was 200 bars ago). GATE for trading: take the bullish tail only when close > SMA(close,200); bearish tail (open/close in LOWER third, close > close[t-200]) only when close < SMA(close,200).
direction: reversal_long (bullish tail above 200MA) / reversal_short (bearish tail below 200MA)
claimed_winrate: none quantified ('not a perfect strategy and many false signals may occur')
sample_or_caveat: Geometry taken verbatim from Sofien's Pine v5 source (two_third_candle_range = (high-low)*0.66; look_to_the_left=200). The 200MA regime gate is the confluence novelty. Note the built-in close vs close[200] term is itself a higher-lookback condition.
source: post:114571898 (Pine source in evidence; entry rule)
pandas_impl:
rng = high - low
upper2_3 = low + 0.66*rng
bull_tail = (close>upper2_3)&(open_>upper2_3)& \
    (close>low.shift(1))&(close<high.shift(1))&(open_>low.shift(1))&(open_<high.shift(1))& \
    (close<close.shift(200))&(rng>rng.shift(1))&(rng>rng.shift(2))
ma200 = close.rolling(200).mean()
long_ok = bull_tail & (close > ma200)

name: Harmonic 5-0 reversal zone + 800-MA support/resistance + RSI(13) confluence (triple gate)
timeframe: 13-RSI on entry TF; 800-period MA = long-term S/R zone; Fib retracement defines the 5-0 reversal zone
condition: Triple confluence LONG: price is inside the bullish 5-0 harmonic reversal zone = retracement of the whole B->C move sits at 50.0% (aggressive) to 88.6% (conservative); AND price is close to the 800-period MA support zone (close near/above SMA800); AND RSI(13) is close to 25%. SHORT mirror: bearish 5-0 zone at 50.0%/88.6% retrace, price near 800-MA resistance, RSI(13) near 75%. All three must align.
sample_or_caveat: The 5-0 swing-pivot detection (B/B2->C/C2 legs, 50%/88.6% Fib) is discretionary/pattern-based and hardest to automate; but the two AUTOMATABLE legs alone form a strong novel gate: |close-SMA800|/close small AND RSI(13) <=25 (long) or >=75 (short). Use that 2-factor reduction if you can't code the 5-0 pivots. No hit-rate.
pandas_impl:
rsi13 = rsi_wilder(close,13)  # 0-100
ma800 = close.rolling(800).mean()
near_ma = (close - ma800).abs() / close < 0.002   # within ~20 pips of the 800MA zone (tune)
long_2of3  = near_ma & (close >= ma800) & (rsi13 <= 25)
short_2of3 = near_ma & (close <= ma800) & (rsi13 >= 75)
# add 5-0 Fib(50%/88.6%) swing-pivot test for the full 3-factor gate

name: 21-period Z-score statistical extreme reversal
timeframe: 21-bar window on the trading TF (use 30m, or compute on 1h/4h as a higher-TF extreme gate)
condition: z = (close - rolling_mean(close,21)) / rolling_std(close,21). LONG when z reaches -2.0 (price 2 std below its 21-bar mean). SHORT when z reaches +2.0. Distinct from %b/range-position because it standardizes by the rolling STD (volatility), not the band width or channel position.
claimed_winrate: none quantified; author warns it 'tends to perform worse in trending markets' and should be regime-checked
sample_or_caveat: Your null list has Bollinger %b and range-position; the rolling Z-score on raw close (mean/std, ddof matters) is a different statistic and the author explicitly pairs it with a trend/range regime check -> i.e. apply only in non-trending regime (e.g. gate by low ADX or by the autocorrelation cooldown rule above). Repeated across two posts.
pandas_impl:
m = close.rolling(21).mean()
s = close.rolling(21).std(ddof=0)
z = (close - m) / s
rev_long  = z <= -2.0
rev_short = z >=  2.0

name: Three-lows-below-5MA exhaustion + 13-bar momentum confirm
condition: BULLISH: the last three lows are each below the 5-period MA of their respective bar (low[t]<MA5[t], low[t-1]<MA5[t-1], low[t-2]<MA5[t-2]) WHILE the current close is back above MA5, AND close[t] > close[t-13] (13-bar momentum still up). BEARISH mirror: last three highs each above their MA5, close back below MA5, AND close[t] < close[t-13].
sample_or_caveat: Combines a short-term exhaustion probe (3 lows piercing MA5) with a reclaim AND a 13-bar trend-alignment filter -> a confluence not in your null list. Causal. No backtest stat.
pandas_impl:
ma5 = close.rolling(5).mean()
below = low < ma5
bull = below & below.shift(1) & below.shift(2) & (close > ma5) & (close > close.shift(13))
above = high > ma5
bear = above & above.shift(1) & above.shift(2) & (close < ma5) & (close < close.shift(13))

name: Normalized 0-100 reversal off 100 with 200-MA position (96702773 strict form)
condition: Identical engine to the overextension rule but stated as the author's exact coded signal: LONG when normalized_distance < 100 AND normalized_distance[t-1] == 100 AND close[t] < close[t-5] AND close[t] < MA200[t]. SHORT when norm<100 AND norm[t-1]==100 AND close[t] > close[t-5] AND close[t] > MA200[t]. Listed separately because this is the verbatim parameterized form (lookback_ma=200, lookback_norm=50) you can paste and test as-is.
sample_or_caveat: Same family as rule above; kept distinct to preserve the EXACT coded thresholds (==100 peak flag, 5-bar momentum, MA200 side). The '==100' flag-value is the kind of indicator-at-a-specific-flag-value gate you asked for.
pandas_impl:
# see normalized-distance impl above; this is the exact flag-value form:
rev_long  = (norm<100)&(norm.shift(1).round(6)==100)&(close<close.shift(5))&(close<ma200)
rev_short = (norm<100)&(norm.shift(1).round(6)==100)&(close>close.shift(5))&(close>ma200)

name: DeMarker(14) oversold/overbought flag gate
timeframe: evaluate on 30m (Kaabar built+charted it on EURUSD hourly; bounds are TF-agnostic)
condition: Compute Kaabar DeMarker on 0-1 scale (NOT the 0-100 TradingView variant). Long flag: DeMarker[t] crosses UP through 0.30 (DeMarker[t] >= 0.30 AND DeMarker[t-1] < 0.30). Short flag: DeMarker[t] crosses DOWN through 0.70. As a pure GATE for your binary: only allow up-bets when DeMarker < 0.30 at decision bar; only allow down-bets when DeMarker > 0.70. Period = 14.
direction: reversal_long below 0.30 / reversal_short above 0.70 (also usable as gate)
claimed_winrate: none given (post defines+backtests but no win-rate stated in corpus); contrarian indicator
sample_or_caveat: Kaabar: 'oversold/overbought values generally set to 0.30 and 0.70'. Note his DeMAX/DeMIN definition divides MA(DeMAX) by MA(DeMAX)+MA(DeMIN), giving 0-1 not 0-100. Author provides no backtest numbers.
pandas_impl:
def kaabar_demarker(df, n=14):
    demax = (df['high'].diff()).clip(lower=0)
    demin = (-df['low'].diff()).clip(lower=0)
    dm = demax.rolling(n).mean() / (demax.rolling(n).mean() + demin.rolling(n).mean())
    return dm  # 0..1 scale; oversold<0.30, overbought>0.70

name: Chande Momentum Oscillator ±65 barrier cross
condition: CMO period=13. Long: CMO[t] <= -65 AND CMO[t-1] > -65 (crosses DOWN into oversold). Short: CMO[t] >= +65 AND CMO[t-1] < +65 (crosses UP into overbought). He explicitly states alternative barriers 50/-50 also valid. As a GATE: only up-bets when CMO < -50; only down-bets when CMO > +50.
sample_or_caveat: Exact code: 'upper_barrier=65, lower_barrier=-65, lookback=13'. He notes 'We establish upper and lower boundaries such as 50/-50 or 65/-65'. CMO bounded -100..+100 so this is a true flag-value, not percentile.

name: Schaff Trend Cycle 25/75 cross with 2-bar confirmation
timeframe: 30m (STC built on MACD 23/50, signal EMA 9; bounded 0-100)
condition: STC bounded 0-100. Long: STC[t] > 25 AND STC[t-1] < 25 AND STC[t-2] < 25 (surges above 25 with prior two bars below 25). Short: STC[t] < 75 AND STC[t-1] > 75 AND STC[t-2] > 75 (plummets below 75 with prior two above 75). Note the asymmetric 25/75 (not 25/75 as OB/OS but as turn-confirmation levels).
direction: momentum_long crossing up 25 / momentum_short crossing down 75
sample_or_caveat: Verbatim: 'Go long whenever the STC surges above 25 with the previous two values below 25. Go short whenever the STC plummets below 75 with the previous two values above 75.' Requires 2-bar lag confirmation -> reduces whipsaw. STC = double-smoothed stochastic of MACD line.

name: CCI(20) ±250 extreme barrier (NOT standard ±100)
timeframe: 30m (CCI is unbounded; Kaabar tuned levels to ±250 by inspecting historical reactions)
condition: CCI period=20. Long: CCI[t] < -250 AND CCI[t-1] > -250 AND CCI[t-2] > -250. Short: CCI[t] > +250 AND CCI[t-1] < +250 AND CCI[t-2] < +250. KEY: he uses ±250, far wider than the textbook ±100 you already null-tested. As a GATE: only up-bets when CCI <= -250; only down-bets when CCI >= +250.

He explicitly says 'the indicator is unbounded... the overbought and oversold levels have to be subjectively found by looking at the historical reactions' and chose ±250. The ±250 (vs ±100) is the novel part you have not tested.

name: Money Flow Index(14) 20/80 cross
condition: MFI(14) bounded 0-100. Long: MFI[t] < 20 AND MFI[t-1] > 20 (crosses down through 20). Short: MFI[t] > 80 AND MFI[t-1] < 80 (crosses up through 80). As GATE: up-bets only when MFI < 20; down-bets only when MFI > 80. Distinguished from RSI by volume-weighting.
sample_or_caveat: From his published Pine: 'buy = mfi<20 and mfi[1]>20; sell = mfi>80 and mfi[1]<80'. Note: you null-tested RSI<20/>80; MFI is volume-weighted so it is a DIFFERENT feature even at the same 20/80 levels.

name: Aroon Oscillator zero-line cross (period 25)
condition: AroonOsc = AroonUp - AroonDown, range -100..+100, period=25. Long: AroonOsc[t] > 0 AND AroonOsc[t-1] < 0 (turns positive). Short: AroonOsc[t] < 0 AND AroonOsc[t-1] > 0 (turns negative). As GATE for a momentum binary: up-bets only when AroonOsc > 0, down-bets only when AroonOsc < 0.
direction: momentum_long zero-cross up / momentum_short zero-cross down
sample_or_caveat: Verbatim: 'Buy whenever the Aroon Oscillator turns positive by surpassing the zero line; Sell whenever it turns negative.' Trend-following (Tushar Chande). Aroon Up/Down = 100*(period - bars_since_extreme)/period.
pandas_impl:
def aroon_osc(df, n=25):
    up = 100*df['high'].rolling(n+1).apply(lambda x: x.argmax(), raw=True)/n
    dn = 100*df['low'].rolling(n+1).apply(lambda x: x.argmin(), raw=True)/n
    return up - dn  # -100..+100; >0 bullish

name: Aroon Oscillator ±75 extreme-reversal variant
condition: Using same AroonOsc(25). Long (mean-reversion): AroonOsc[t] > -75 AND AroonOsc[t-1] < -75 AND AroonOsc[t-2] > -75 (rebounds out of deep-down -75 zone). Short: AroonOsc[t] < 75 AND AroonOsc[t-1] > 75 AND AroonOsc[t-2] < 75 (rejects out of deep-up +75 zone). This is his SECOND, distinct Aroon signal function using ±75 extremes rather than zero.
direction: reversal_long out of -75 / reversal_short out of +75
sample_or_caveat: From his alternate signal code: 'if AroonOsc[i] > -75 and AroonOsc[i-1] < -75 and AroonOsc[i-2] > -75: buy'. Distinct from the zero-cross rule above; he ships both.

name: Coppock Curve x Stochastic-25 confluence gate
timeframe: daily/4h Coppock for regime, 30m Stochastic for timing (he overlays both)
condition: TWO-CONDITION GATE. Coppock CC = WMA(10) of (ROC14 + ROC11) of close. BULLISH GATE fires only when BOTH: (1) CC crosses from negative to positive (CC[t]>0 AND CC[t-1]<=0); AND (2) Stochastic %K (14) is in the ~25 area (i.e. <=25 / pulling back). Only take up-bets when this joint condition holds. Symmetric short = CC turns negative AND stochastic ~75.
sample_or_caveat: Verbatim: 'A bullish signal is confirmed whenever the CC surpasses zero (turns positive) and the stochastic oscillator is at the 25 area.' The stochastic-25 requirement is the confluence filter that he says makes 'the CC strategy much more interesting.' Stochastic standard levels 20/80; he uses 25 as the pullback area.

name: Ultimate Oscillator x Stochastic double-extreme confluence
condition: TWO-CONDITION GATE. Long: 14-period Stochastic %K reaches/<=25 AND Ultimate Oscillator < 35 AT THE SAME BAR. Short: Stochastic %K reaches/>=75 AND Ultimate Oscillator > 65 at the same bar. Both must agree on overextension. UO uses Larry Williams 7/14/28 buying-pressure/true-range weighting.
sample_or_caveat: Verbatim: 'Go long whenever the 14-period Stochastic reaches 25 while the Ultimate Oscillator is below 35 at the same time; Go short whenever Stochastic reaches 75 while UO is above 65.' Note UO 35/65 are tighter than its usual 30/70.
pandas_impl:
def ultimate_osc(df, s1=7, s2=14, s3=28):
    bp = df['close'] - pd.concat([df['low'], df['close'].shift()],axis=1).min(axis=1)
    tr = pd.concat([df['high'],df['close'].shift()],axis=1).max(axis=1) - pd.concat([df['low'],df['close'].shift()],axis=1).min(axis=1)
    avg=lambda n: bp.rolling(n).sum()/tr.rolling(n).sum()

import numpy as np
def _atr_wilder(df, n=10):
    h,l,c = df['high'],df['low'],df['close']
    pc = c.shift(1)
    tr = np.maximum(h-l, np.maximum((h-pc).abs(),(l-pc).abs()))
    return tr.ewm(alpha=1/n, adjust=False, min_periods=n).mean()

def supertrend(df, period=10, mult=1.25):
    # Sofien's exact recursive band logic (causal). Returns the SuperTrend line.
    atr = _atr_wilder(df, period)
    hl2 = (df['high']+df['low'])/2.0
    ub = hl2 + mult*atr   # basic upper
    lb = hl2 - mult*atr   # basic lower
    c = df['close'].values; ubv=ub.values; lbv=lb.values
    n=len(df); fub=np.zeros(n); flb=np.zeros(n); st=np.zeros(n)
    for i in range(1,n):
        fub[i] = ubv[i] if (ubv[i]<fub[i-1] or c[i-1]>fub[i-1]) else fub[i-1]
        flb[i] = lbv[i] if (lbv[i]>flb[i-1] or c[i-1]<flb[i-1]) else flb[i-1]
    for i in range(1,n):
        if st[i-1]==fub[i-1] and c[i]<=fub[i]: st[i]=fub[i]
        elif st[i-1]==fub[i-1] and c[i]>fub[i]: st[i]=flb[i]
        elif st[i-1]==flb[i-1] and c[i]>=flb[i]: st[i]=flb[i]
        elif st[i-1]==flb[i-1] and c[i]<flb[i]: st[i]=fub[i]
        else: st[i]=fub[i]
    return pd.Series(st, index=df.index)

def vama(df, short=3, long=55, k=0.2):
    vs=df['close'].rolling(short).std(ddof=0)
    vl=df['close'].rolling(long).std(ddof=0)
    alpha=(k*(vs/vl)).clip(0,1).fillna(0).values
    c=df['close'].values; n=len(c); out=np.full(n,np.nan)
    start=long
    out[start]=c[start]
    for i in range(start+1,n):
        out[i]=alpha[i]*c[i]+(1-alpha[i])*out[i-1]
    return pd.Series(out,index=df.index)

condition: Take only bullish divergences when close is ABOVE the 800-period simple moving average (reversal_long, but trend-aligned); take only bearish divergences when close is BELOW the 800-period SMA (reversal_short). A softer variant uses 'long-term MA below market price' as the bullish filter.
sample_or_caveat: This is the 'only counter-trend-fade WITH the higher-timeframe trend' filter. 800-SMA on 30m ~ 16.7 trading-days of trend context. Distinct from the multi-EMA confluence you already nulled because it is a SINGLE very-slow MA used purely as a sign gate on divergence pivots, not an EMA stack.

name: K's Doji (3-bar) + 14-period stochastic extreme
timeframe: any; author shows on intraday EURUSD
condition: Exact 3-bar structure. reversal_long (bullish): bar[-2] bearish (close[-2] < open[-2]), bar[-1] is a doji (open[-1] == close[-1], use tolerance abs(open-close) < 0.0001 for FX), current bar bullish (close > open), AND 14-period stochastic < 20. reversal_short (bearish): bar[-2] bullish (close[-2] > open[-2]), bar[-1] doji, current bar bearish (close < open), AND 14-period stochastic > 80. NOTE the Pine code indexes as close>open & close[1]==open[1] & close[2]<open[2] i.e. doji is the MIDDLE bar, confirmation is the CURRENT bar.
claimed_winrate: No numeric win-rate published for this combo.
sample_or_caveat: This is a SPECIFIC FLAG-VALUE gate: not 'doji anywhere' but doji-as-middle-bar of a 3-bar reversal sandwich AND a momentum extreme. The strict open==close in Pine must become abs(open-close) < tol on real FX (Kaabar's own Python uses abs(O-C)<0.0001). Reuse across 42707530, 121183773, 143256141.
source: rule:42707530:20 / rule:143256141:15, code post:143256141:code:1 (Stochastic Doji Finder Pine), Python tol post:46568331:code:8-9
pandas_impl:

body=(d['close']-d['open']).abs()
doji_prev = body.shift(1) < tol
bull_doji = (d['close']>d['open']) & doji_prev & (d['close'].shift(2)<d['open'].shift(2)) & (stoch14 < 20)
bear_doji = (d['close']<d['open']) & doji_prev & (d['close'].shift(2)>d['open'].shift(2)) & (stoch14 > 80)
# stoch14 = stoch_raw(d,14) ; all shifts are causal

name: K's Doji + 1-sigma Bollinger break (Bollinger Doji)
condition: Same 3-bar K's-doji structure but the location gate is a 20-period Bollinger band built with ONE standard deviation (not 2). reversal_long: bull doji structure AND current close < lower band (SMA20 - 1*stdev20). reversal_short: bear doji structure AND current close > upper band (SMA20 + 1*stdev20).
sample_or_caveat: The 1-standard-deviation band (vs your already-nulled 2-sigma %b extremes) is the untested knob: a 1-sigma break is far more frequent, so it acts as a mild location filter on the doji rather than a rare extreme. Reuse posts 108752238, 126114742, 139808960.

name: K's Doji + 50-MA trend (trend-aligned doji)
condition: Doji on smoothed 'K-candlestick' chart (OHLC each replaced by its own N-period MA) WITH 50-period MA trend filter. Simplified testable form: a doji (abs(open-close)<tol) while close > 50-period MA = momentum_long bias; doji while close < 50-MA = momentum_short bias. The Python uses K-candles where O,H,L,C are each a 'lookback'-period moving average and the doji is abs(MA_close - MA_open) < 0.0001 with high<=low-avg ordering checks plus current MA-open < MA-open 3 bars ago.
sample_or_caveat: Two non-standard elements: (1) doji is a TREND-CONTINUATION gate here (with the 50-MA), opposite to the stochastic-doji reversal; (2) the 'K-candlestick' smoothing replaces raw OHLC with MAs of OHLC before detecting the doji - a noise-reduction trick worth testing as its own feature. There is also a 'one-signal-per-cluster' guard (my_data[i-1,9]==0).

kbody=(kc-ko).abs()

name: Alpha Pattern - fractal higher-low / lower-high swing reversal (5/13/21 lookback)
condition: AUTHORITATIVE = the Pine code (prose in the article is mis-stated). reversal_long (buy_pattern): low < low[5] AND low < low[13] AND low > low[21] AND close > close[3]. i.e. price is making a fresh short-term low vs 5 and 13 bars ago BUT is still ABOVE the low of 21 bars ago (a forming higher-low / failed deeper breakdown) AND has upside momentum vs 3 bars ago. reversal_short (sell_pattern): high > high[5] AND high > high[13] AND high < high[21] AND close < close[3].
claimed_winrate: No numeric hit-ratio in the published post text.
sample_or_caveat: STRONG candidate you almost certainly have NOT tried - it is NOT the NR7/fractal you nulled. The published prose says 'lower than the low 21 periods ago' but the Pine source says low > low[21] (and sell uses high < high[21]); the CODE is the ground truth and gives a failed-breakdown / higher-low reversal, not a momentum breakout. The close>close[3] term is a built-in 3-bar momentum confirmation. Fib-spaced lookbacks 5/13/21 with mixed inequality directions is the non-obvious structure.
source: rule:45582154 / 49218458 (Finding & Coding a Market Pattern), code post:45582154:code:2 (Alpha Pattern Pine)

name: Double-bottom / double-top (W-M) structural reversal (Kaabar two-pivot)
condition: Detected via the same two-trough scan as divergence but on PRICE PIVOTS defined by an oscillator crossing a barrier. reversal_long (double bottom): two consecutive bottoms (each = oscillator dips below lower_barrier then recovers) where the SECOND bottom's price is HIGHER than the first (second bottom higher-low) -> bullish. The bearish-divergence twin: two bottoms where the second is LOWER (classic deeper double-bottom retest). reversal_short (double top): two tops where the second is HIGHER (M-top, second top higher-high) -> 'bearish trend in progress' sell; or second top LOWER = exhaustion top. Author explicitly pairs 'two bottoms second higher = buy' and 'two tops second lower = continuation sell'.
sample_or_caveat: This is the W/M detector you have not tried because it is OSCILLATOR-ANCHORED (the two pivots are validated by stochastic/RSI re-crossing a barrier within `width` bars), not raw-price peak-finding. The barrier re-cross is what makes the two bottoms 'confirmed swing lows' rather than every wiggle. Same width=60 default.

name: TD Setup 9 (DeMark) momentum-exhaustion reversal counter
timeframe: evaluate on 30m and as a HTF gate on 4h/daily
condition: Buy Setup (reversal_long context): a bullish price flip then 9 CONSECUTIVE bars each with close < close[4] (close lower than the close four bars earlier). On the 9th such bar = TD Setup 9 buy (downside exhaustion, watch for bounce). Sell Setup (reversal_short context): 9 consecutive bars each with close > close[4]. The count resets if any bar fails the close-vs-4-bars-ago condition.
claimed_winrate: No numeric win-rate; author frames TD9 as a probabilistic exhaustion flag, 'works best with confirmation.'
sample_or_caveat: Pure structural counter, no indicator params to overfit - ideal as a GATE/feature on the 30m binary OR as a higher-TF condition (count TD9 on 4h/daily, trade the 30m in that direction). The count value itself (1..9) is a usable integer feature, not just the terminal 9.

name: TD Countdown 13 (DeMark) deep-exhaustion reversal (after a completed Setup)
condition: After a Buy Setup 9 completes, begin Buy Countdown: count (not necessarily consecutive) bars where close <= low[2] (close at or below the low TWO bars earlier). reversal_long fires at the 13th such bar with the qualifier: low of countdown-bar-13 <= close of countdown-bar-8. Sell Countdown: count bars where close >= high[2]; reversal_short at 13th with high of bar-13 >= close of bar-8.
claimed_winrate: No numeric win-rate; described as 'more developed exhaustion signal' than TD9.
sample_or_caveat: Distinct trigger from the Setup (close vs low[2], not close vs close[4]) and the bars need NOT be consecutive, with a specific bar13-vs-bar8 qualifier. This is a precise, fully-specified structural reversal flag rarely tested on FX 30m. Use as gate/feature; the running countdown integer 1..13 is itself a feature.
